video.title: Google Veo 3 Just Changed the Game: Here’s Your Money-Making Tutorial

summary: Chris Koerner gives a tutorial-style roundup of ways to make money with Google's Veo 3 video model ($250/month, half off for the first 3 months). Ideas include white-label AI video for production agencies, AI UGC for small ecom brands, realtor promos, stock footage, productized monthly reel packages for niche local businesses, upselling into $1k/month content retainers, prompt packs ($29), micro-courses ($49), a paid newsletter or community, and licensing your voice on ElevenLabs. He gives specific cold-DM scripts (an opt-in ask to agency owners on personal Instagram) and a 5-step 'start with $250' plan: 3 demos, 30 DMs, a $100 test video, reinvest, then a $500/month offer. He also cites a viral Reddit post where a creator now quotes $10-15k for Veo commercials. Most figures are hypothetical pricing suggestions rather than results the host has achieved. Much of the outreach relies on cold DMs, which would hit UK PECR limits when the targets are individuals or sole traders.

speakers.name: Chris Koerner
speakers.description: Host of The Koerner Office; serial entrepreneur, newsletter operator

ideas.name: White-label AI video production for video and marketing agencies
ideas.one_liner: Generate ads, B-roll and UGC-style clips with Veo 3 for production agencies, which resell them to their clients while you stay behind the scenes.
ideas.business_model: Per-video fees or a monthly white-label retainer
ideas.customer: Video production companies and marketing agencies (local or national; found via Google, Clutch, Upwork)
ideas.problem: Agencies pay crews for low-margin shoots and risk losing clients to AI tools; most are not using AI yet
ideas.offer: Demo videos made for the agency's existing clients, then ongoing AI-generated ads, B-roll and UGC content delivered white-label

pricing.notes: Agencies' clients reportedly pay $5-10k per video.

acquisition_channels.details: DM agency owners on personal Instagram with an opt-in ask ("I just made a video for your client, can I send it?"), then share a Google Drive folder and follow up persistently. UK PECR: unsolicited marketing DMs, texts or emails to individuals or sole traders need prior consent. Cold email to limited companies is OK with an opt-out. Personal Instagram DMs to agency owners are risky, so prefer their company email or LinkedIn.

quote.text: don't overlook DMing the owner of these agencies on Instagram because they're getting cold emailed all day long
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

acquisition_channels.details: Short non-pitchy message offering examples and pointing to savings on low-budget shoots.

quote.text: Hey not sure if your team is experimenting with AI video tools yet but I've been using Google's new VO model and it's nuts
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

ideas.delivery: Prompt Veo 3 for 5-10 second polished clips with background music; deliver via Google Drive or Vimeo with no branding; agency handles the client.
unit_economics_claims: One agency client could be $1-4k per month
Reddit creator: $500 in credits and half a day vs $500k commercials

acquisition.how: Agency research and demos need manual tailoring; DM/email sending could be templated, but PECR limits cold DMs to individuals.

delivery.how: Veo generates clips; a human curates, edits and polishes.

uk_applicability.notes: UK agencies are a fair market. Cold email to Ltd agencies is fine; personal Instagram DMs to owners are unsolicited electronic marketing to individuals under PECR. Disclose AI use and mind ASA rules on AI ads.

risks: Rapid commoditisation as AI video tools spread
Agencies may adopt the tools themselves

quotes.text: You're just piggybacking on their book of business on their success You're just offering them a way to do it cheaper faster and easier
quotes.speaker: Chris Koerner

quotes.text: One of these agency clients could turn into $1 to $4,000 a month every month without having to interact with their clients
quotes.speaker: Chris Koerner

quotes.text: go to their website find their portfolio find a couple of their clients and generate two to three VO videos promoting their clients and send it to them
quotes.speaker: Chris Koerner

ideas.name: AI UGC and ad videos for small ecommerce brands
ideas.one_liner: Sell AI-generated UGC-style videos for Facebook, Instagram, TikTok and Shorts ads to small online brands.
ideas.customer: Small online brands: Shopify stores, fitness, skincare, supplements, coaching
ideas.problem: Brands need constant video content and are tired of filming it themselves or paying thousands a month
ideas.offer: AI-made UGC with no actors or cameras, styled to the brand

pricing.notes: Host says the per-video range ('1 to300') likely means $100-300; test pricing models.

acquisition_channels.details: Send DMs with demo videos and sell one video to get a case study. UK PECR: unsolicited marketing DMs, texts or emails to individuals or sole traders need prior consent. Cold email to limited companies is OK with an opt-out. Personal Instagram DMs to agency owners are risky, so prefer their company email or LinkedIn.

quote.text: So move now test fast Send a bunch of DMs Sell one video Now you have a case study Then you can scale it
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

ideas.delivery: Veo 3 prompts; ChatGPT for prompt writing.

acquisition.how: Outreach manual; PECR limits cold DMs to sole traders.

uk_applicability.notes: UK DTC brands buy UGC. AI-generated 'UGC' that implies real customers may mislead under the CAP Code and CMA rules on fake reviews and testimonials, so label it as AI.

risks: Fake-testimonial or misleading-ad risk if AI people pose as real customers

quotes.text: you offer them AI made UGC user generated content No paid actors no cameras no real people but it looks exactly like real people

quotes.text: You could charge 500 to $1,000 a month for four to eight different videos

ideas.name: AI cinematic promo videos for realtors
ideas.one_liner: Use Veo to generate drone-style flyovers, interior B-roll and lifestyle shots for estate agents, much cheaper than a shoot.
ideas.problem: Agents pay hundreds or thousands for promo videos
ideas.offer: Cinematic AI property and neighbourhood videos

uk_applicability.notes: UK property ads must not mislead (CPRs, Property Ombudsman/ASA). AI-generated interiors or flyovers that don't show the real property are high risk. Lifestyle B-roll only.

risks: Low trust in AI visuals for real listings

quotes.text: You can use VO to generate cinematic drone flyovers interior B-roll even like neighborhood lifestyle shots

pricing.notes: Host argues flat monthly beats per-video ($50/video) pricing.

Personal Instagram DMs to agency owners are risky, so prefer their company email or LinkedIn.

tactics.name: Opt-in DM before pitching
steps: Find an agency's client from their portfolio
Make a Veo video for that client
DM the owner asking if you can send it
Send a Google Drive link once they agree
Follow up persistently. UK PECR: use company email for Ltd agencies, not unsolicited personal DMs.

quote.text: Hey I know you have insert brand name as a client I just made a video for them Do you mind if I send it to you to see what you think
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

tactics.name: Weekend demo portfolio
steps: Pick three niches (fitness, food, fashion/lifestyle)
Write very specific cinematic prompts
Render 5-10 second clips with music
Upload unbranded to Google Drive or Vimeo

quote.text: Make each one of these in your portfolio about 5 to 10 seconds Use background music Polish it up Upload it to Google Drive or Vimeo with no branding
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

tactics.name: Reverse-engineer prompts from the Sora Explore page
steps: Go to sora.com Explore, filter by top month and video
Copy the prompts behind the best videos
Paste a dozen into ChatGPT and ask for the first principles that make them work

quote.text: Don't look at the videos look at the prompts that generated them and there is so much you can learn there
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

tactics.name: Flat monthly pricing over per-unit
steps: Package a fixed number of videos per month at one price
Productize: one offer, one deliverable, one price
Sell via a landing page and Stripe link

quote.text: You could say $50 a video and that is less enticing than $500 per month for 10 videos I promise you people just want to know what the bill is
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

tactics.name: $250 start plan
steps: Buy Veo
Make 3 ad-quality demos
Cold DM 30 (15 agencies, 15 brands)
Offer a $100 test video with 48-hour turnaround
Reinvest in the next 30 DMs by niche
Package into a $500/month offer after 2-3 paid videos. Check PECR before cold DMs to UK individuals and sole traders.

quote.text: follow up with anyone who replies and offer a test video for 100 bucks No meetings no contracts
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

tactics.name: Anchor the upsell against a pricier alternative
steps: After the first paid video, ask to handle the rest of their content
Offer a bundled package
Compare the price with a social media manager costing 2-4x

quote.text: And your pitch you're contrasting this against a social media manager that might cost two to four times that
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

tactics.name: Niche and reuse
steps: Serve one vertical at a time
Reuse prompt structures and the landing page across clients in that vertical
Copy the landing page to the next niche

quote.text: You can literally copy and paste the landing page especially if you use something like card or web flow
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

warnings.warning: The early-mover edge will erode within 6-12 months as competition arrives.

quote.text: in six months to 12 months people won't be shocked and you'll have more competition So if you're going to make a move make it now
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

warnings.warning: Don't over-explain the tech to agencies; just show results.

quote.text: don't try to overexlain the tech because that just makes them feel dumb and they won't want to respond because of their ego
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

warnings.warning: Expect many rejections; it's a numbers game.

quote.text: In fact a lot of them will say "No thank you." But it's just a numbers game
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

warnings.warning: UK PECR (extractor note): the cold DM and text tactics aimed at individuals, sole-trader trades and agency owners' personal Instagram are unsolicited electronic marketing without consent. Use company email for limited companies, or in-person or phone outreach screened against TPS/CTPS.
AI 'UGC' that looks like real customers may be misleading advertising (ASA/CMA); disclose AI-generated content (extractor note).

lessons.lesson: The AI tool isn't the product; the packaged offer is.

quote.text: You see VO is a tool but your offer is the product
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

lessons.lesson: Selling through agencies lets you piggyback on their client base while they handle client management.

quote.text: You just deliver the content and get paid You're the ghost in the machine
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

lessons.lesson: Visual products need a demo; a text pitch alone won't land.

quote.text: So a cold email or text or whatever by itself is not going to do You've got to show them something
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

lessons.lesson: Ask permission to send the sample; an agreed opt-in makes the prospect feel obliged to watch.

quote.text: you want them to opt in to getting pitched That is always more effective than just pitching them
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

lessons.lesson: Flat, predictable monthly pricing beats per-unit pricing.

quote.text: Here's why I like simple flat fee offers Because people want to know what their bill is at the end of the month
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

lessons.lesson: Specialising in one niche lets you reuse content and prompts, halving the work.

quote.text: Make a couple changes and your work just got cut in half
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

lessons.lesson: Land one paid job quickly to get a case study, then scale.

quote.text: Start with one demo one DM land one paid video That's it You're in Now you got a case study
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

lessons.lesson: Use the first sale as a foot in the door to upsell a full content retainer.

quote.text: you're trying to move from freelancer to partner because at the end of the day most of your clients don't just want videos they want results
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

lessons.lesson: Document everything while learning; it becomes course material.

quote.text: while you're learning these things record your screen Why would you not document everything you're doing
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

lessons.lesson: Many traditional agencies aren't using AI yet; Twitter is a bubble.

quote.text: if you're on Twitter a lot Twitter is a bubble Most of these agencies are not deep into AI yet
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

evidence_quality.rationale: Hype-driven roundup recorded days after launch. Nearly all pricing and income figures are hypothetical suggestions or hearsay (a Reddit post, voice-licensing earnings). The host reports no Veo revenue of his own; only the newsletter subscriber count is first-hand.
evidence_quality.promotional_conflict: Promotes the host's newsletter (tkopod.com) and community (tkowners.com).
